faqs.question: What is the eligibility criteria for admission to top Dental colleges in India?
faqs.answer: The eligibility criteria for best Dental schools in India vary from course to course. Refer below the course-wise eligibility criteria for top Dental Universities in India : Eligibility Criteria for best BDS Colleges in India: Candidates should pass Class 12 in the Science stream with Physics , Chemistry , and Biology as core subjects They should obtain a minimum 50 percent aggregate (General category students) and 45 percent (reserved category candidates) Their age should range between 17 years and 25 years They should qualify for NEET Eligibility Criteria for best MDS Colleges in India: Candidates should have a BDS degree from a dental college/institute recognised by Dental Council India They must have completed their Internship for BDS before taking admission to the MDS course Candidates should secure a minimum 55 percent aggregate of all subjects of the BDS course They should qualify for the MDS entrance exam Eligibility Criteria for Diploma Dental Colleges in India For undergraduate Dental Diploma courses, candidates should pass Class 12 with a minimum 50 percent aggregate They must have studied Science stream, with Physics, Chemistry, and Biology/ Biochemistry as core subjects in Class 11 and Class 12 Postgraduate dental Diploma should have completed BDS or undergraduate Dental Diploma course and completed a compulsory rotatory internship by the time of admission Eligibility Criteria for Certificate Dental Colleges in India Candidates should complete a bachelor’s level Dental course from a recognised institute They should complete the compulsory rotatory internship followed by the course completion Disclaimer: This information is sourced from official website and may vary.

faqs.question: Is specialisation mandatory after a dental course?
faqs.answer: Specialization is not mandatory after completing a general Dental course . Graduates can practice as general dentists immediately after earning their degree and completing required internships. However, pursuing a specialisation in areas like orthodontics, prosthodontics, or oral surgery can enhance career prospects, increase earning potential, and allow dentists to handle more complex cases. It is a choice based on career goals rather than a requirement.

faqs.question: How can I pursue Dental courses after Class 12th?
faqs.answer: Studying Dental courses after completing Class 12 (or its equivalent) typically involves pursuing a BDS or Dental Medicine. Here's a step-by-step guide on how to pursue Dental courses after Class 12 in India: Ensure Eligibility: Generally, candidates must have completed Class 12 with a Science stream ( Physics , Chemistry, Physics ,2 Biology), with a minimum aggregate score in these subjects as specified by the respective dental colleges or universities. Appear for Entrance Exams: Dental colleges in India usually admit students based on national or state-level entrance exams. Some of the common entrance exams for undergraduate dental courses include NEET . Apply for BDS : Once you have made sure that you are eligible for BDS, you can apply for the graduate course online after researching for the best possible university for yourself. Complete BDS: Once you secure admission to a dental college, pursue the BDS courses. The duration of the undergraduate dental course is typically four to five years, including a one-year internship.

faqs.question: Is Dental course hard to pursue?
faqs.answer: Dental school can be nearly as challenging as Medical school. The considerable amount of studying required of dental school students causes many of them to suffer. It contains a wealth of Dental knowledge that must be applied in practice in addition to being memorised. The fact that Dental school students start using Dental procedures practically far earlier than their Medical school colleagues is a significant distinction between Dental school and Medical school. Within the first two years of dental school, practical courses are utilised. This may increase the stress that students already experience as a result of their demanding academic schedules and challenging exams.

faqs.question: Are Dental courses theory-heavy or practical-focused?
faqs.answer: Dental courses strike a balance between theory and practice. While foundational knowledge in anatomy, physiology, and dental materials is theory-based, students spend significant time in labs and clinics. Practical sessions involve hands-on training in procedures like cavity filling, tooth extraction, and oral hygiene management. This ensures that graduates are competent in real-world dental practice while understanding the scientific principles behind treatments.

faqs.question: Do Dental courses require prior Science knowledge?
faqs.answer: Yes, a background in science, particularly biology, is important for Dental courses . Knowledge of subjects like chemistry, physics, and biology helps in understanding oral anatomy, physiology, and pharmacology. Students with a strong Science foundation can grasp dental concepts faster and perform better in practical sessions. However, training in dental techniques also equips learners to develop clinical skills irrespective of minor gaps in prior knowledge.

faqs.question: Do dental courses cover preventive as well as corrective dentistry?
faqs.answer: Yes, Dental courses emphasize both preventive and corrective dentistry. Preventive training teaches oral hygiene, routine checkups, and early detection of dental issues to avoid future problems. Corrective dentistry involves treatments like cavity fillings, root canals, prosthodontics, and orthodontic procedures. A combination of both ensures graduates can maintain oral health in patients while addressing existing dental conditions effectively.

faqs.question: Can syllabus differ between colleges for the same Dental course?
faqs.answer: Yes, while Dental courses follow guidelines set by the Dental Council of India (DCI), the syllabus can vary slightly between colleges. Differences may include elective subjects, research opportunities, lab facilities, and teaching methods. Core topics like anatomy, oral pathology, and clinical practice remain standard, ensuring students acquire essential knowledge and skills regardless of the college.

faqs.question: Can dental course graduates work abroad?
faqs.answer: Yes, Dental graduates can work abroad, but most countries require licensing exams and registration with local dental councils. Additional requirements may include language proficiency, credential verification, or completing certain clinical hours. Graduates can pursue clinical practice, research, teaching, or healthcare consultancy, but preparation for international licensing is essential for smooth transition.

faqs.question: Are there opportunities in dental healthcare administration?
faqs.answer: Yes, Dental graduates can explore careers in healthcare administration. Roles may include managing dental clinics, hospital departments, or public oral health programs. Administrative positions require a combination of dental knowledge and management skills. Graduates can contribute to policy-making, patient management systems, quality control, and training programs while supporting the broader healthcare infrastructure.

faqs.question: Can I use the title 'Dr.' after completing my Dental degree?

blocks.value: Yes, dentists in India with a Doctor of Dental Medicine (DMD) or Doctor of Dental Surgery (DDS) degree are legally permitted to use the term "Doctor" or "Dr." before their names. This is due to the DMD and DDS degrees being seen as similar to medical degrees such as the Doctor of Medicine ( MD ).

It is crucial to note, however, that the usage of the title "Dr." is governed by the Dental Council of India (DCI), India's governing organisation for dental education and practice. The DCI has precise norms and restrictions for dental professionals' usage of titles.

faqs.question: What is the difference between dental courses and dental technician courses

blocks.value: Dental courses focus on training dentists to diagnose, treat, and manage oral health issues, including surgeries and complex procedures. They combine clinical practice with theory in oral medicine, orthodontics, and preventive care.

Dental technician courses, however, are more lab-oriented. They teach students to fabricate dental prosthetics, crowns, bridges, and other appliances. Technicians work under dentists rather than treating patients directly.

faqs.question: How much emphasis is given to practical sessions in Dental courses?

blocks.value: Practical sessions are a core part of Dental education. Students spend significant hours in laboratories and clinics, performing procedures under supervision.

Hands-on training ensures students are skilled in patient examination, restorative treatments, minor surgeries, and preventive care. The practical focus bridges the gap between theory and real-world dental practice, preparing graduates to handle clinical responsibilities effectively.

blocks.value: Dental courses or Dentistry is the branch of Medicine that deals with the prevention and treatment of oral disorders, such as diseases of the teeth and their supporting structures and diseases of the mouth's soft tissues. Dentistry also includes diagnosing and treating jaw malformations, tooth misalignment, and congenital defects of the oral cavity, such as cleft palate. Dental specialities and subspecialties include orthodontics and paediatric dentistry, dental orthopaedics, oral and maxillofacial surgery, periodontics, public health dentistry, prosthodontics, endodontics, oral and maxillofacial pathology, and oral and maxillofacial radiology, in addition to general practice.
DFP-Banner

Take a look at the important information regarding the Dental course in terms of admission, college, syllabus and scope.

value: Admission through NEET: The admission to Dentistry courses across India is conducted through the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET). Upon qualifying for the exam by clearing the cutoff, candidates will have to participate in the counselling process conducted by national and state-level admission authorities.

Duration: The duration of the Dentistry course depends upon the level of the programme. The UG level Dentistry programme or Bachelor of Dental Surgery (BDS) is of five years duration including one year of internship. On the other hand, Master in Dental Surgery (MDS) programme is of three years.
Dentistry Course Evaluation Pattern: Students are marked based on the internal exams, projects, vivas, lab exercises and internships.

Scope of Dentistry: A practitioner in Dentistry might work in various areas. A dentist is usually called in to undertake dental identification of an unknown individual or confirm the identification of a deceased person. In recent years, dentistry has provided excellent job options. Dental problems have become a widespread issue affecting people from all walks of life. Procedures for treatment have gotten more specialised as science and technology have progressed. As a result, the career is both difficult and financially rewarding, attracting new aspirants. Dentistry is a discipline of study that deals with dental care and treatment.

Typical Core Dental Subjects

value: General pathology refers to a broad and complicated field that studies the mechanisms underlying cell and tissue injury as well as how the body responds to and repairs harm. Necrosis, neoplasia, inflammation, wound healing, and how cells respond to harm are some of the topics that may be researched.

Microbiology is the study of bacteria, algae, viruses, slime moulds, fungi, and protozoa, which are tiny organisms. Most other biological investigations do not use the tools used to examine and manipulate these tiny, mainly unicellular creatures.

Oral Microbiology discusses biofilms on oral surfaces comprising tens or hundreds of distinct species, all of which interact and contribute to the system's overall function. The biofilm interacts with the host tissues as well as external influences including nutritional intake and smoke inhalation.

Preclinical operative dentistry is a part of operative dentistry in which students receive hands-on training on dummy models in a simulated oral environment for tooth preparation and restoration using various materials.

Oral pathology is the study, diagnosis, and treatment of disorders affecting the gums, teeth, joints, bones, skin, glands, and muscles around the mouth. According to the American Dental Education Association, Oral Pathologists need an average of 37 months of advanced education to become experts in their speciality.

In dentistry, pharmacology is crucial. The goal of dental pharmacology is to comprehend the scientific aspects of how medications used in dentistry interact with the human body's numerous systems. Pharmacology includes pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics, which are two aspects of drug metabolism.

Therapeutic dentistry is a type of treatment that tries to improve the health of the teeth and gums. In common dental therapeutics are dedicated to preserving, restoring, and maintaining the health of your oral cavity through therapeutic procedures such as periodontal therapy and tooth extraction.

blocks.value: Typical Elective Subjects for Dentistry

value: Public health dentistry is concerned with identifying critical dental health problems and developing practical solutions to improve the dental health of populations rather than individuals.

Conservative dentistry and endodontics are the branches of dentistry that deal with the treatment of caries, misshapen, discoloured, unesthetic, or shattered teeth, while endodontics deals with the treatment of pulpal and periapical illnesses, as well as the management of dental pain.

Periodontics is a dental speciality that focuses on the supporting structures of teeth as well as diseases and ailments that impact them. The cementum, alveolar bone, gingiva, and periodontal ligament are all part of the periodontium, which is made up of supporting tissues.

Paediatric and Preventive Dentistry is committed to the oral health of children from infancy through adolescence, with the experience and qualifications to care for a gums, child's teeth, and mouth at all phases of development.

Dentofacial orthopaedics is concerned with the guidance of facial growth and development, which happens primarily throughout childhood, and is one of the reasons why children are often the greatest candidates for dentofacial orthopaedic therapy.

Endodontics is that branch of dentistry that deals with the dental pulp and tissues that surround the tooth's roots. "Endo" means "within," and "odont" means "tooth." The delicate pulp tissue inside the tooth is treated by endodontic treatment, often known as root canal therapy.

Prosthodontics is a discipline of dentistry that deals with the replacement of lost teeth and the soft and hard tissues that go with them using prosthetics that can be fixed or detachable, or supported and kept by implants.

Because Dentistry is such a broad field with so many specialities, students need to refer to a wide variety of literature during their undergraduate or postgraduate studies. Some of the most often recommended novels are listed below.

value: David A. Mitchell and Laura Mitchell

In a condensed format, the latest version of this pocket handbook covers the field of clinical dentistry. It has been totally changed and updated to include a plethora of fresh information, such as web-based learning and relevant resources, as well as more diagrams and colour clinical images.
BSAVA Manual of Canine and Feline Dentistry and Oral Surgery

The BSAVA Manual of Canine and Feline Dentistry and Oral Surgery is a timely publication in an internationally increasing speciality subject. It is a valuable resource for general small animal veterinary surgeons, students, and nurses/technicians who want to improve their knowledge and skills in dentistry and oral surgery.
Basic Guide to Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery

The role of the dental nurse in oral and maxillofacial surgical operations is explained in detail in Basic Guide to Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery. Anatomy of the head and neck, pain and anxiety control, injuries and more complex procedures are all covered in an easy-to-understand manner.
Quick Reference to Dental Implant Surgery

Quick Reference to Dental Implant Surgery provides busy practitioners with quick access to all of the key information needed for effective dental implant surgery. It has been deliberately developed to be utilised while the patient is seated and follows a simple, easy-to-follow pattern.
Color Atlas of Dental Implant Surgery

With this colourful atlas-style book, you'll be able to learn implant processes and methods in no time! Dental Implant Surgery includes full-colour clinical photographs and practical guidance for a wide range of implant difficulties. Treatment planning, pre-surgical recommendations, thorough surgical techniques, and postoperative follow-up are all included in this guide.

blocks.value: Entrance Exams for Dentistry

The purpose of the Dental Entrance Exams is to get admission to the Bachelors of Dental Surgery (BDS) and Masters of Dental Surgery (MDS) programmes. Aspirants can easily pass the entrance exam if they prepare according to the syllabus and previous papers. Candidates must focus on their studies in order to be the first to pass the tests. The eligibility requirements for various colleges may differ.

Following your BDS, you may want to pursue an MDS to gain a more in-depth understanding of the subject. It is the highest level of study in the field of dentistry and can help you find a career as a dentist in reputable organisations.

You can enrol in either a government or private college based on your performance in the entrance test. Depending on your interests, you can select a specialisation area. Prosthodontics, orthodontics, operative dentistry, and conservative dentistry are some of the specialisation possibilities available during the MDS.
Dental Syllabus for Distance Learning Programmes

Distance education is a viable option for those who cannot afford full-time classes. Part-time or distance Dentistry programmes are also available to students who do not meet the eligibility requirements for full-time courses. Distance learning programmes have a syllabus that is strikingly comparable to traditional programmes. The evaluation method is essentially identical to that of conventional courses, with 30 per cent for internal assessment and 70 per cent for the end-of-semester examination. Top schools which offer distance learning programs in Dentistry are IGNOU , Symbiosis Centre for Distance Learning (SCDL) , and Gitam Deemed to be University to name a few.
